# Disagreement Log — 2 Maccabees Chapter 9
**Date:** 2026-03-17
**Agents:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Total Disagreements:** 18

---

## V.1 — "retreated in disorder" vs. "made his retreat in disgrace" vs. "was being driven out in humiliating retreat"
- EMET: "retreated in disorder"
- LOGOS: "made his retreat in disgrace"
- PNEUMA: "was being driven out in humiliating retreat"
- SOPHIA: "retreated in disgrace" — LOGOS phrasing preferred; PNEUMA's passive construction is interpretive

## V.4 — "judgment of heaven" vs. "heaven's judgment" vs. "God's justice"
- EMET/LOGOS: "judgment of heaven" (literal)
- PNEUMA: "God's justice" (interpretive substitution)
- SOPHIA: "judgment of heaven" — retain the Greek *krisis*; PNEUMA's substitution loses the impersonal framing

## V.5 — "all-seeing Lord" vs. "all-seeing Lord" vs. "the Lord — the all-seeing God of Israel"
- EMET/LOGOS: "the all-seeing Lord, the God of Israel"
- PNEUMA: expands with dash construction
- SOPHIA: EMET/LOGOS phrasing retained as more precise

## V.5 — "irremediable pain in his bowels" vs. "irremediable pain seized his bowels" vs. "savage, unrelenting pain ripped through his bowels"
- EMET: "an irremediable pain in his bowels seized him"
- LOGOS: "an irremediable pain seized his bowels"
- PNEUMA: "a savage, unrelenting pain ripped through his bowels" (strong paraphrase)
- SOPHIA: LOGOS phrasing — "irremediable" must be retained; PNEUMA's "savage" replaces a key word

## V.6 — "indeed very justly" vs. "fittingly so" vs. "a just punishment"
- EMET: "And indeed very justly"
- LOGOS: "And fittingly so"
- PNEUMA: "A just punishment" (adds noun not in Greek)
- SOPHIA: "And fittingly so" — concise; EMET's "indeed very justly" is slightly awkward

## V.7 — "breathing fire in his passion" vs. "breathing out fire in his fury" vs. "seething with murderous rage"
- EMET/LOGOS: retain the fire/breathing metaphor
- PNEUMA: "seething with murderous rage" — loses "fire" metaphor
- SOPHIA: "Breathing fire in his passion" — metaphor must be retained

## V.7 — "every member of his body" vs. "every joint of his body" vs. "every joint in his body"
- EMET: "every member"
- LOGOS/PNEUMA: "every joint"
- SOPHIA: "every joint" — more precise anatomically; Greek *melos* can mean limb or joint in context of a fall

## V.8 — "superhuman arrogance" vs. "superhuman arrogance" vs. "boasted"
- EMET/LOGOS: "superhuman arrogance" (literal *hyperphanon phronema*)
- PNEUMA: omits the compound term, paraphrases with "boasted"
- SOPHIA: "superhuman arrogance" — this specific term is important to the author's rhetoric

## V.9 — "worms swarmed out of" vs. "worms swarmed up out of" vs. "worms began pouring out of"
- EMET: "swarmed out"
- LOGOS: "swarmed up out"
- PNEUMA: "began pouring out" (softer?)
- SOPHIA: "swarmed out of" — EMET phrasing; "swarmed" is vivid and accurate

## V.9 — "flesh fell off" vs. "flesh began to rot away" vs. "flesh rotted off"
- EMET: "his flesh fell off"
- LOGOS: "his flesh began to rot away"
- PNEUMA: "his flesh rotted off"
- SOPHIA: "his flesh fell away" — Greek *apepipten*: fell/dropped off; LOGOS's "rot away" is interpretive

## V.10 — "touch the stars of heaven" vs. "reach the stars of heaven" vs. "touch the stars of heaven"
- LOGOS: "reach"
- EMET/PNEUMA: "touch"
- SOPHIA: "touch" — Greek *haptesthai*: touch/grasp; LOGOS's "reach" is acceptable but less precise

## V.12 — "subject to God" vs. "subject to God" vs. "submit to God"
- EMET/LOGOS: "be subject to God"
- PNEUMA: "submit to God"
- SOPHIA: "be subject to God" — Greek *hypotassesthai*: be subordinate to; PNEUMA's "submit" is acceptable

## V.13 — "vile man" vs. "vile man" vs. "wretched man"
- EMET/LOGOS: "vile man" (Greek *miare* — polluted, defiled)
- PNEUMA: "wretched man" (loses the ritual-pollution connotation)
- SOPHIA: "vile man" — *miare* has a specific religious defilement sense; "wretched" is too morally neutral

## V.15 — "not even to count worthy of burial" vs. "not even to count worthy of burial" vs. "planned to throw unburied"
- EMET/LOGOS: retain Greek construction with "count worthy"
- PNEUMA: paraphrases with "planned to throw unburied"
- SOPHIA: LOGOS phrasing — the legal/formal register of "count worthy" is part of the contrast with "citizens of Athens"

## V.16 — "sacred vessels" vs. "sacred vessels" vs. "sacred vessels he had stolen"
- PNEUMA adds "he had stolen" — not in Greek, though contextually implied
- SOPHIA: omit addition; let the text speak for itself

## V.17 — "become a Jew" vs. "become a Jew" vs. "convert to Judaism"
- EMET/LOGOS: "become a Jew" (literal)
- PNEUMA: "convert to Judaism"
- SOPHIA: "become a Jew" — the Greek *Ioudaios genesthai* is precise; retain literal

## V.28 — "murderer and blasphemer" vs. "murderer and blasphemer" vs. "Antiochus the murderer and blasphemer"
- PNEUMA adds the name for clarity
- SOPHIA: omit name addition; the Greek does not repeat it and the epithet stands alone effectively

## V.29 — "foster brother" vs. "foster brother" vs. "foster brother"
- All three agree: *syntrophos* = "foster brother"
- Minor disagreement: LOGOS adds "conveyed the body home" where EMET says "took the body back"
- SOPHIA: "conveyed the body home" — slightly more formal
